summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most videos get 1,200-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best performers are short Hindi videos with a surprising claim about a robot or sensor ('doesn't see, only hears/feels'), especially clap switch, gyro, PIR and IR robot topics. Generic 'How does X work?' videos on everyday devices (taps, doors, smoke alarms, touchscreens) get far less reach, and the one English video and the newest untested upload have almost no results.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about a robot or Arduino-style sensor, with a bold counterintuitive hook ('X ke bina robot gir jaata', 'Clap switch taali nahi, shor sunta hai', 'Sensor dekhta nahi, mehsoos karta hai'). Titles state a surprising fact or negation in plain Hinglish, use one emoji, and end with #shorts. Maker-style topics (robots, clap switch, mic, line follower) beat public-place devices (mall door, washroom tap, street light). YouTube only gets a few hundred views on the strongest of these, so Instagram is the main platform.
doMore: Make surprising 'it doesn't X, it actually Y' hooks about robots and sensors, the format behind your top 8 videos
Do follow-ups on clap switch, gyro, IR and PIR topics, since each of these topics has already had 500+ views on at least one platform
Pick maker-relevant topics (robot, Arduino module, mic, line follower) over everyday public devices
Post Instagram first and treat YouTube as secondary; test what lifts YouTube, e.g. gyro, clap and PIR titles that already got 500+ views there
End with a question or a 'save this for your project' prompt to lift saves and shares, which are low on most videos
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' titles on everyday devices (tap, door, smoke alarm, street light)
Publishing English videos while the channel audience is Hindi, and uploads that skip Instagram
